learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; an unresolved fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: identify the approach
items.prompt: A model explains a pattern using genetic vulnerability, learned threat expectations, and ongoing housing instability. Which approach is represented?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: purpose of classification
items.prompt: Which is a defensible introductory purpose of psychological-disorder classification?
options: Prove one complete cause for every classified person.
Replace an individual assessment with a family label.
Organize patterns for communication and research.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: read prevalence
items.prompt: A survey reports that 80 of 4,000 sampled adults meet its stated case definition during one year. What is the one-year prevalence in that sample?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: compare matched rates
items.prompt: Study A finds 120 cases among 6,000 people; Study B finds 90 among 3,000 using the same interval and case definition. Which sample has the higher proportion?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: incidence versus prevalence
items.prompt: A cohort excludes existing cases at baseline and records newly emerging cases during the next 12 months. Which type of measure is described?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: audit a rate comparison
items.prompt: Two reports show 4% and 7%, but one uses lifetime self-report and the other uses clinician-rated cases during one month. What is the best interpretation?
options: The percentages are not directly comparable.
The 7% report proves the population has greater biological risk.
The 4% report must contain a calculation error.
The percentages can be compared because both use a percent sign.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: distinguish an existing-case measure
items.prompt: A survey asks which residents currently meet a case definition on one specified day. Which measure is being estimated?
options: Incidence rate over a follow-up interval
Lifetime risk of ever developing the condition
New-case proportion after excluding baseline cases
Point prevalence in the defined population
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: distinguish a new-case measure
items.prompt: A campus registry removes students with existing cases at enrollment and counts first-onset cases during the semester. Which measure is described?
options: Period prevalence including all existing cases
A causal effect of enrollment on the condition
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: four fields for a rate
items.prompt: Which set is required to interpret and compare a reported disorder rate?
options: Cases and a disorder-family name only
Sample size and one causal explanation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compare new-case data
items.prompt: Cohort X records 30 new cases among 3,000 at-risk people; Cohort Y records 24 among 1,200 over the same year with the same definition. Which has higher incidence proportion?
options: Neither, because incidence never uses a denominator
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: obsession and compulsion
items.prompt: A fictional vignette describes intrusive contamination thoughts and repeated washing used to reduce the resulting distress. Which introductory family is the closest match?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: event linkage
items.prompt: After a severe accident, a fictional character has recurring event-related intrusions and avoids reminders. Which family best organizes the stated linkage?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: physical-symptom distress
items.prompt: A fictional case reports persistent physical symptoms plus extensive distress and repeated health-related checking. The prompt does not say the symptoms are fabricated. Which family is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: elevated-energy episode
items.prompt: A fictional character has a distinct period of unusually elevated mood, markedly increased activity, and little perceived need for sleep. Which family is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: psychosis and disorganization
items.prompt: A fictional presentation centers on hallucination-like experiences, fixed false beliefs, and disorganized speech. Which introductory family is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: compare two records
items.prompt: Record A centers on gaps in autobiographical memory and disrupted identity continuity. Record B centers on an enduring inflexible interpersonal pattern across settings. Which pairing is correct?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: choose the organizing feature
items.prompt: Which feature most specifically distinguishes a depressive-family presentation in this introductory matrix?
options: Intrusive thoughts followed by repetitive rituals
Sustained low mood or loss of interest
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: depressive pattern
items.prompt: A fictional vignette emphasizes persistent low mood and markedly reduced interest in previously valued activities. Which family is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: separate worry from compulsion
items.prompt: Which contrast best separates anxiety-family worry from an obsessive-compulsive pattern?
options: Physical symptom distress versus trauma linkage
Broad fear or worry versus obsession-linked ritual
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: anxiety pattern
items.prompt: A fictional case centers on excessive worry across several ordinary domains, with no rituals, trauma linkage, psychosis, or mood elevation stated. Which family is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: bounded evidence claim
items.prompt: A group study finds a dopamine-signaling difference associated with schizophrenia. Which statement is best supported?
options: The measure diagnoses every participant with certainty.
Dopamine signaling may contribute to the disorder.
One transmitter completely explains every presentation.
Biological evidence is irrelevant to schizophrenia.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: Parkinson’s mechanism
items.prompt: Degeneration reduces dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra. Which functional prediction is most direct?
options: Every memory trace is immediately erased.
A clinical diagnosis is proven from this sentence alone.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: Alzheimer’s memory context
items.prompt: Which pairing is most consistent with introductory Alzheimer’s biological evidence?
options: Stable lifelong personality style with no neural change
Brief worry caused only by one upcoming event
Dopamine-neuron loss limited to movement circuits only
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: depression evidence limit
items.prompt: A depression study reports differences in stress-response and monoamine-related systems at the group level. Which conclusion is warranted?
options: One chemical deficit diagnoses each individual.
Social and psychological variables cannot matter.
The findings prove one treatment works for everyone.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: identify the strongest claim
items.prompt: Researchers observe a neural-circuit difference more often in a disorder group than in controls, with substantial overlap between groups. What is the strongest claim?
options: The circuit measure perfectly classifies every person.
The circuit difference is the only possible cause.
The observation has no scientific relevance.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: match four evidence records
items.prompt: Which evidence-to-disorder pairing is most direct at introductory depth?
options: Amyloid and tau pathology → uncomplicated temporary worry
One monoamine measure → certain depression diagnosis
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: association is not diagnosis
items.prompt: Which phrase correctly reports a group-level biological finding?
options: The finding proves the disorder in any individual.
The finding is the sole cause in all cases.
The finding is associated with the disorder group.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: overlapping distributions
items.prompt: A biomarker average differs between groups, but many values overlap. Which inference is justified?
options: The marker separates every individual without error.
The marker may inform a group-level mechanism.
The marker establishes one complete causal pathway.
The marker determines treatment for each person.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: disorder–mechanism map
items.prompt: Which introductory map is accurate?
options: Schizophrenia: one transmitter explains all cases
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compare mechanisms
items.prompt: Record A describes progressive memory decline with neurodegenerative pathology. Record B describes loss of substantia nigra dopamine neurons with movement effects. Which pairing fits?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
